Name of the Surah

• It is called Hud, because the name of the Prophet of Allah, Hud (peace be upon him), is mentioned in it five times, and because more of what is related about him is found in it than in any other surah.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Affirming the first task of the Prophet (ﷺ), which is calling to Tawhid (monotheism), warning of punishment for those who deny it, and giving the good news of bliss to those who believe in it, and establishing this through the evidences that point to Allah's miraculous power and the wonders of His creation.

• Mentioning the accounts of the Messengers, to strengthen the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the face of the hardships and terrors he encounters, and to console him with what happened to his brother Messengers of various kinds of trial, so that he may take them as an example, and to strengthen his certainty along with those who believed in him, so that their hearts are not constricted by the deniers and the mockers.

• Explaining the unity of the call of the Prophets and Messengers, and pointing out that the foundation of the misguidance of the misguided is their lack of fear of Allah's punishment in the Hereafter, due to their disbelief in the Resurrection and the Recompense.

• Mentioning a miraculous proof of the truthfulness of the Prophet's (ﷺ) message, through narrating about the previous nations, such as the people of Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut, Shu'ayb and Musa (peace be upon them), and what occurred between them and their prophets, as an indirect reminder of the lessons contained in all of that.

• Affirming the Gathering (al-Hashr), and informing that Allah is aware of the hidden secrets of people, that He manages the affairs of every creature, and that people will return to Him, and He will recompense them for what they did.

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra.﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters has already been covered at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah. This Book which Allah sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ), its verses have been made firm, free from defect and falsehood, then they were made clear with commands and prohibitions and the explanation of what is lawful and unlawful, from Allah, the All-Wise in managing affairs, the All-Aware of what their outcomes will lead to.

The revelation of the Qur'an, the explanation of its rulings, their detailing, and their being made firm, is so that you worship none but Allah, alone, with no partner. Indeed I am, O people, a warner to you from Allah, warning you of His punishment, and a bringer of good tidings, giving you good news of His reward.

Ask Him to forgive you your sins, then turn back to Him in repentance; He will let you enjoy good provision in your worldly life, with a good life in it, until your appointed term comes. And He will give every person of merit in knowledge and deed the full reward for his merit, without any deficiency. But if you turn away from what I call you to, then I fear for you the punishment of a severe day, namely the Day of Resurrection. This is a severe warning to whoever turns away from the commands of Allah the Exalted and denies His messengers.
Return to Allah is your destination after your death, all of you together, so beware of His punishment. And He, glorified is He, is able to resurrect you, gather you, and recompense you.

Indeed, these polytheists conceal disbelief in their breasts, thinking that what their souls harbor is hidden from Allah. Do they not know that when they cover their bodies with their garments, Allah does not conceal from Him their secret and their open deeds? Indeed, He is All-Knowing of everything that their breasts hold within, of intentions, inner thoughts, and innermost secrets.

God has undertaken to provide the sustenance of every creature that crawls upon the face of the earth, out of His bounty. He knows its place of settling during its life and after its death, and He knows the place where it will die. All of this is written in a Book with God that clearly records all of it.

It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was over the water before that, so that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed. And that which is best in deed is what is done sincerely for Allah and in accordance with what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) followed. And if you, O Messenger, say to these polytheists of your people, "Indeed, you will be resurrected alive after your death," they will hasten to deny it and say, "This Qur'an that you recite to us is nothing but clear magic."

And if We defer the punishment from these disbelievers until a known term, they will surely say, mocking and denying: "What is preventing it from coming?" Yet on the day it comes upon them, nothing will turn it away from them, and no one will repel it; and the punishment they used to mock will surround them on every side.
